messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: algebraic number field construction forcing all triangle areas to share a common lower bound

Generate 10 candidate conjectures within that direction, sampled from the
full distribution of responses you could give. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "Place 13 points at coordinates (α^i mod 1, α^(i+13) mod 1) for i=0,...,12, where α = (1+√5)/2. Every triangle area equals |det M|/2 where M is a Fibonacci circulant matrix with entries in Z[√5], and the minimal determinant magnitude over all 286 triples is exactly (3-√5)/2, giving minimum triangle area (3-√5)/4 ≈ 0.19098.", "probability": 0.085}, {"conjecture": "Choose α = 2^(1/3) in the cubic field Q(2^(1/3)). Place points p_i = (α^i mod 1, α^(i+13) mod 1) for i = 0,...,12. Each triangle area is a Q-linear combination of {1, α, α^2} with integer coefficients bounded below by the minimal nonzero norm in the Minkowski embedding, yielding minimum triangle area ≥ 1/(6√3) ≈ 0.0962, and computational verification confirms exactly 1/(6√3).", "probability": 0.078}, {"conjecture": "Use the real subfield of the 13th cyclotomic field Q(ζ_13 + ζ_13^(-1)) of degree 6. Place points at (Tr(α·ζ^i)/c, Tr(β·ζ^i)/c) for i=0,...,12 with α, β algebraic integers and c a normalizing constant. All triangle areas are traces of cyclotomic integers with norm ≥ 1, giving minimum area exactly 1/(2·13·sin(2π/13)) ≈ 0.0883 after optimal choice of α, β.", "probability": 0.072}, {"conjecture": "Place 13 points at the algebraic-integer lattice points (Tr(ω^i · θ_j), Tr(ω^i · θ_j^2)) scaled into [0,1]², where ω = e^(2πi/13) and θ_j = ζ_13^j for j=0,...,12. Every triangle area is a positive integer multiple of the regulator of Q(ζ_13) divided by a fixed denominator, so the minimum area is exactly R_13 / (2·13^2) where R_13 is the regulator, computable to be approximately 0.075.", "probability": 0.069}, {"conjecture": "Select 13 points forming the orbit of (cos(2π/13), sin(2π/13)) under the Galois group Gal(Q(ζ_13)/Q), embedded in R² via the canonical Minkowski map restricted to a 2-dimensional subspace. All triangle determinants are algebraic integers in Q(ζ_13) with complex absolute value ≥ 1 under every embedding, giving minimum area exactly 1/(2·φ(13)) = 1/24 ≈ 0.0417 after optimal linear scaling into the unit square.", "probability": 0.064}, {"conjecture": "Use the field Q(√13) with fundamental unit ε = (3+√13)/2 having norm -1. Place 13 points at (Tr(ε^i · α)/d, Tr(ε^i · β)/d) for i=0,...,12 with α, β chosen as small algebraic integers and d the diameter of the orbit. Triangle determinants are norms of elements of Z[√13], bounded below by 1, giving minimum area 1/(2d²) where d = Tr(ε^6) ≈ 50, yielding minimum area ≈ 0.0002. This is suboptimal but rigorously certified.", "probability": 0.058}, {"conjecture": "Take the degree-13 totally real field K = Q(θ) where θ is a root of x^13 - x^12 - 1. Place point i at the normalized pair (σ_i(θ), σ_i(θ^2)) for i=1,...,13 where σ_i are the 13 real embeddings. Every triangle area equals |det(σ_i(θ^j))_{j=0,1,2}|/(2·D) where D is the field discriminant. The minimal such determinant over all triples is exactly 1 by the algebraic integer property, giving minimum area 1/(2D) where D = disc(x^13 - x^12 - 1) = 13^13 - 12^12 ≈ 2.1×10^14.", "probability": 0.053}, {"conjecture": "Construct 13 points using a 2-dimensional projection of the Leech lattice's automorphism group: place points at the images of the 13 projective points of PG(1,12) under a quadratic map into [0,1]² defined over Q(√13). All triangle areas are of the form (a + b√13)/c with a,b,c integers satisfying a² - 13b² ≥ 1 (Pell equation), so the minimum area is exactly (√13 - 3)/(2·13) ≈ 0.0301, achieved by the fundamental solution to the Pell equation.", "probability": 0.047}, {"conjecture": "Use a (13, 4)-BCH code over GF(3) and lift codewords to R² via the Minkowski embedding of Q(ζ_13). The 13 points correspond to the 13 cyclic shifts of the generator polynomial's coefficient vector, embedded as (Re(ζ^i·g(ζ)), Im(ζ^i·g(ζ))) for a degree-4 generator g. All triangle areas are determinants of circulant matrices over Z[ζ_13] with entries ±1, bounded below by 1/√13 in absolute value, giving minimum area 1/(2√13) ≈ 0.1387.", "probability": 0.041}, {"conjecture": "Place 13 points at (σ_1(α_i), σ_2(α_i)) where α_i = θ^i for i=0,...,12, θ is a root of the Hilbert class polynomial of discriminant -163 (degree 3, but the construction uses the degree-13 extension Q(θ, θ^(1/13))), and σ_1, σ_2 are two real embeddings. All triangle determinants are norms in the compositum, bounded below by the product of local norms ≥ 1, giving minimum area exactly 1/(2·163^(13/2)) which is negligibly small but rigorously positive. The construction proves the algebraic lower bound principle but does not optimize the constant.", "probability": 0.035}]}
